chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdillah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them).

He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) laughed one day until his molar teeth were visible. Then he said: Will you not ask me why I laughed? They said: Of course, O Messenger of God. He said: I am astonished at the affair of the Muslim person — there is nothing that God, Mighty and Majestic, decrees for him except that it is good for him in the end of his affair.

key_terms.عَاقِبَة: The ultimate outcome or end result of an affair — emphasizes long-term perspective over short-term appearance
key_terms.قَضَاء: Divine decree or judgment — refers to what God ordains for a person, encompassing both what appears good and what appears difficult
key_terms.نَوَاجِذ: The molar (back) teeth — their visibility indicates a full, wide smile or hearty laughter, marking the unusual nature of this occasion

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about divine decree being good for the Muslim?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) laughed until his back teeth showed, then invited his companions to ask why. When they did, he expressed astonishment at the blessed state of the believer: every divine decree, no matter how it appears, ultimately serves their good. This hadith was transmitted through the family of Imam al-Sadiq back to the Prophet, reflecting the Shia chain of transmission through the Imams. The concept of divine decree (qada') here emphasizes tawakkul and trust in Allah's wisdom, especially meaningful in contexts of hardship.
